name: Landscape of Grand Pré
description: Grand Pré is a stretch of flat farmland on the Minas Basin in Nova Scotia, reclaimed from the sea by Acadian settlers in the 1600s. They held back some of the world's highest tides, which average 11.6 metres, with earth dykes and wooden sluice gates called aboiteaux. Those dykes still protect the fields today. The area also memorializes the Acadians' deportation, which began in 1755.
